title: An SSD stores bits as trapped electrons

probes.question: In a flash cell, what holds the stored charge?
options: A floating gate insulated all around

probes.question: True or false: multi-level cell flash stores more than one bit in each memory cell.

image.alt: Close-up of a black NAND flash memory chip with its many metal pins on a green circuit board.

body.claim: An SSD stores your data as electric charge trapped inside tiny memory cells.
body.why: Each flash cell has a floating gate that is insulated all around, so electrons placed on it stay trapped. The charge changes the cell's threshold voltage, and that is how a bit is read back. Multi-level cells store more than one bit each. SSDs have no moving parts.
